newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday on a technical correction after surges in the past few days but the rates were still at high levels due to continued new domestic A share issues and listings, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract fell sharply to 18.48 percent from 28.00 percent on Wednesday.
Turnover rose to 14.63 million lots from 13.03 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The falls today were a technical correction, with the rates very high after successive surges," said one trader.
"But the rates are still high, with more new domestic A shares in the offing," he added.
Six companies are issuing or listing on Shanghai's A share market this week, attracting large amounts of funds from the repo market and traders expect rates to stand firm on Friday.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Thursday, with major institutions liquidating positions in existing shares to prepare for a new seven-year bond issue scheduled to start on Friday, trader said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 122.95 yuan from 123.47 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 2.15 million lots from 4.93 million.
Traders believe the spot market will remain weak in the short term during the issue of the seven-year bond which will last until November 20.
